title: I made a boring game
author: fireweb2
selftext:
The goal is to make a game that feels different from other tidying and organizational games.  
I don't want the player to have traditional objectives, skills to unlock, progression systems, or a grid-based placement system. Instead, the idea is to give the player complete freedom to pick up objects and place them wherever they want  
However, I feel that the game is currently too boring. By removing objectives, progression, and other traditional game mechanics, I may have removed too much. Right now, the core interaction is enjoyable for a while, but there isn't enough to keep the player engaged.

  
How can I improve this slop game ? 

  
IA was use only for the main capsule. I'll solve it later.

  
Thanks for your time

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5215190/PotionsTidy/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5215190/PotionsTidy/)

  
If you need I can give you Steam key for immediat playtest.

comments.author: woodysixer
comments.body:
Is this a joke? You “made a game” that removes everything that actually makes something a game, and you’re surprised that it’s boring? 

Give the player a goal. That’s literally the one requirement for something to even be a game.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body:
I still have some little features 😄 



\- Stepladder for placing objects up high

\- Secret room to unlock

\- An unlockable potion that allows you to pick up items two at a time

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
what you have is basically a simulation since you removed "objectives, progression, and other traditional game mechanics"

you can introduce more mechanics to retain players e.g. maybe mixing potions lead to something happening. 

it boils down to literally giving players stuff to do at this point because there is no progression etc. 

assume you have a player who is curious enough to try everything once in your game/simulation, then you can get a rough estimation of the player's play time based on the number of activities and the duration of each activities. That would be the "ceiling" since the average player probably isn't that curious

it is possible for players to keep doing the same activity, but they would have to have a reason i.e. maybe they find the game charming/cozy or whatever

TLDR; just give players more stuff to do. that's it
